paragraphs.text: Joel Pedraza Villaseñor participated in Seizure NLD-11-01 on 2011-09-15. Círculo del Valle Quieto was linked to Seizure NLD-11-01 on 2011-09-15. Seizure NLD-11-01 occurred at Nuevo Laredo on 2011-09-15. A taxi operator with regular fares at the Nuevo Laredo freight yards reported that inspectors on the commercial bridge recovered 12 kg of cocaine from a passenger vehicle that had been following a tractor-trailer of Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte, and that the yards attributed the load to Pedraza, the Reynosa plaza boss known as El Diez. The operator described the load as a small escort consignment that was meant to draw inspection away from the trailer.

Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte supported Seizure NLD-11-01 on 2011-09-15. Joel Pedraza Villaseñor used DEMO-TEL-00165 on 2011-09-15. Seizure NLD-11-01 transited Highway 85 route on 2011-09-15. The operator stated that the trailer itself crossed without inspection and that the trucking firm's dispatcher described the loss as acceptable. The telephone identifier above was the one the operator had heard Pedraza give to a driver at the yards. The operator stated that the vehicle and trailer had come up the highway from Monterrey together.

Círculo del Valle Quieto controlled Highway 85 route from 2010-09-01 until 2019-05-23. Aurelio Castañón Vidaurri led Círculo del Valle Quieto from 2010-09-01 until 2019-05-23. Joel Pedraza Villaseñor was a member of Círculo del Valle Quieto from 2010-09-01 until 2020-01-10. The operator characterized the highway between Monterrey and the border as the network's own, with its trucks moving unchallenged and rival crews paying to use it. Castañón was described as the head of the network and Pedraza as a founding member. The reporting office assesses the operator as having incidental access through conversations at the yards and notes that the escort consignment tactic is consistent with other reporting on this crossing.
